holidays.name: National Lazy Day
holidays.description: This is the one day a year when doing nothing counts as an achievement. Skip the chores, cancel the ambitious plans, and lie on the couch without guilt. Your to-do list can wait until tomorrow.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on August calendars, at the sleepy peak of summer.
holidays.funFact: Many holiday calendars list National Lazy Day on August 10 every year, so you can plan your napping well in advance.

holidays.name: National S'mores Day
holidays.description: This day honors the campfire trio of toasted marshmallow, melted chocolate and crunchy graham cracker. You can make them over a fire, on a stovetop, or in the microwave. Just be ready for sticky fingers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance whose exact origin is unclear. It celebrates a treat that has been a camping favorite for about a century.
holidays.funFact: The first known published s'mores recipe appeared in a 1927 Girl Scout guide, under the name 'Some More.'

holidays.name: World Lion Day
holidays.description: This day is a roar of appreciation for the big cats of the savanna. It raises awareness about the threats lions face and the need to protect them. Many people mark it by learning about lion conservation or supporting wildlife groups.
holidays.origin: Big Cat Rescue founded World Lion Day in 2013 to draw attention to lion conservation.
holidays.funFact: Fewer than 25,000 wild lions are thought to remain in Africa and India, which is why the day carries an urgent conservation message.
